heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1S requires upgrading to a hardened steel nozzle and extruder gears before safely printing abrasive Polymaker PA6-CF. Once upgraded, it delivers exceptional structural parts at a safe maximum print speed of 131 mm/s capped by an 11 mm³/s volumetric flow limit.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with PVP glue stick or Magigoo PA as a release and adhesion agent
slicerTweaks: Cap Max Volumetric Speed at 11 mm³/s in the Filament Settings tab to avoid under-extrusion at high travel rates.
Set Hotend Temperature to 290°C for all layers and Bed Temperature to 45°C with the chamber door closed.
Disable auxiliary cooling fans completely and set the part cooling fan threshold to 0% min and 20% max to prevent inter-layer delamination.
Configure a 5mm outer brim with 0.1mm brim-object gap to secure corners and eliminate warping on high-infill functional parts.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe stringing, rough fuzzy surface finish, and popping sounds at the nozzle
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excess moisture absorption; PA6 is extremely hygroscopic and degrades quickly in ambient air.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the spool in a filament dryer at 80-100°C for 8 to 12 hours before printing, and print directly from a sealed dry box.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Extruder clicking, rapid flow drop, and partial clogging during extrusion
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Carbon fiber agglomerations catching in a worn or standard stainless steel nozzle, or abrasive wear on the stock drive gears.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Upgrade hotend assembly to Bambu Hardened Steel 0.4mm (or 0.6mm) and install hardened extruder drive gears.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Corner lifting and warping from the bed plate mid-print
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Inadequate bed adhesion due to lack of PA-specific adhesive or thermal shock from excessive cooling fans.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a uniform layer of Magigoo PA or PVP glue stick on the Textured PEI plate, maintain bed temp at 45°C, and keep auxiliary/chamber cooling fans turned off.

faq.question: Can I print Polymaker PA6-CF with the stock Bambu Lab P1S hotend?
faq.answer: No. The stock P1S comes with a stainless steel nozzle and stainless steel extruder gears, which abrasive carbon fiber will quickly erode. You must install the Bambu Hardened Steel Hotend and Hardened Extruder Gear Assembly.

faq.question: Can I feed Polymaker PA6-CF through the Bambu AMS?
faq.answer: Polymaker PA6-CF is stiff and highly abrasive, which can wear down the internal plastic funnels and PTFE tubes of the AMS. It is strongly recommended to feed directly from an external drybox.

faq.question: Why is the recommended bed temperature set to only 45°C?
faq.answer: Polymaker engineered their PA6-CF to utilize low bed temperatures (40-50°C) with dedicated adhesives to mitigate thermal contraction gradients and prevent warping without requiring extreme bed heat.

faq.question: Do I need to anneal Polymaker PA6-CF parts after printing?
faq.answer: Yes, for maximum tensile strength, impact resistance, and heat deflection resistance (up to ~215°C), anneal the finished print in an oven at 80-100°C for 8 to 16 hours.
